findings.description: sign_out_everywhere catches StoreError per record, logs a warning and carries on, so it only returns a smaller count. change_password ignores whether every session was ended, even though its docstring promises that. If the file store fails to write, the old sessions stay valid after a password change (for example a stolen access or refresh token) and the caller is never told. The count returned does not reveal this, since the caller does not know how many sessions existed.
findings.suggestion: Re-raise or aggregate failures from sign_out_everywhere, or have it report failures to the caller, so change_password fails loudly when any session could not be revoked.
findings.title: change_password silently leaves sessions alive when revocation fails

findings.description: _read_all catches OSError, ValueError and KeyError and returns {}. A corrupt file, a transient read error, or a record missing a field makes the store look empty. The next save, delete or take_by_refresh then rewrites the file from that empty dict, permanently wiping every other session. A single malformed record also discards all valid ones.
findings.suggestion: Treat only FileNotFoundError as empty. Raise StoreError for other read or parse failures, and skip or quarantine individual bad records instead of dropping the whole file.
findings.title: Corrupt or unreadable session file is treated as empty and then overwritten

findings.description: FileSessionStore.get and all read the file without taking self._lock. The writer uses a fixed temp name and os.replace, so reads never see a partial file. However, sign_out_everywhere and purge_expired iterate over a snapshot from all() and delete records afterwards, and a concurrent refresh can have already rotated the record, so the delete targets a stale hash. Separately, MemorySessionStore.get reads the dict without the lock.
findings.suggestion: Take the lock in get and all, or document and accept the snapshot semantics. Prefer a store-level delete_by_user operation that runs atomically under the lock.
findings.title: Unlocked reads race with non-atomic temp-file writes

findings.description: take_by_refresh removes the record before the expiry and active checks. If the refresh token is expired, or the user is deactivated, the session is already deleted. More importantly, if _issue then fails with a StoreError on save, the old session is gone and no new one exists, so the user is logged out with no way to retry.
findings.suggestion: Handle failure of _issue by restoring the old record, or perform the take and the save in a single store transaction.
findings.title: Refresh token consumed before validation; failed refresh destroys the session

findings.description: purge_expired calls delete in a loop without handling StoreError. One failed write aborts the purge after some deletions, and the caller gets an exception instead of a count. On FileSessionStore each delete re-reads and rewrites the whole file, so purging N sessions costs O(N²) I/O.
findings.suggestion: Add a bulk delete to the store, or catch StoreError per record as sign_out_everywhere does.
findings.title: purge_expired aborts on the first store error and stays quadratic on the file store
